stories.title: Omololu Falobi (1971–2006): 20 years of an enduring legacy
stories.author: Gbenga Osinaike
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Omololu Falobi (1971–2006): 20 years of an enduring legacy
stories.summary: Gbenga Osinaike remembers the journalist and AIDS advocate, two decades after his death.
briefing: Writing on the twentieth anniversary of Omololu Falobi’s death, Gbenga Osinaike revisits a colleague’s life in journalism and public service. The tribute recalls the shock felt at The Punch when news of Falobi’s death reached the newsroom.
The original opinion piece reflects on Falobi’s work with Journalists Against AIDS and the legacy he left behind. Read Osinaike’s full remembrance in the original publication.

stories.title: ANLCA @ 72: Stakeholders Seek Digital Transformation and Better Trade Facilitation
stories.author: Derin Adeogun
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: ANLCA @ 72: Stakeholders Seek Digital Transformation and Better Trade Facilitation
stories.summary: Nigeria’s maritime stakeholders discuss technology, port efficiency and the future of customs brokerage.
briefing: Derin Adeogun reports on the seventy-second anniversary of the Association of Nigerian Licensed Customs Agents. Speakers at the Lagos event discussed the role of customs agents in trade and the changes facing their profession.

The report covers calls for better coordination, digital processes and improvements to cargo movement. It brings together remarks from government representatives, maritime organisations and industry leaders.

stories.title: How a family sponsored multimillion naira building for teenagers in Abuja Church
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: How a family sponsored multimillion naira building for teenagers in Abuja Church
stories.summary: Sam Oye recounts a family’s offer to support a dedicated space for young people.
briefing: The Transforming Church’s lead pastor, Sam Oye, describes how a family offered to fund a building for teenagers at the Abuja church. His account connects the proposed project to questions about young people’s place in church life.
The original report presents the pastor’s testimony and his reflections on people who support projects intended to make a lasting difference. The account is attributed to his message.

stories.title: Sowore holds private meeting with Pastor Adeboye, recounts his encounter
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Sowore holds private meeting with Pastor Adeboye, recounts his encounter
stories.summary: The politician shares his account of a meeting with the RCCG general overseer after a thanksgiving service.
briefing: Church Times reports on Omoyele Sowore’s account of attending a thanksgiving service and meeting Pastor Enoch Adeboye. Sowore described the visit in a social-media post and said Adeboye offered to pray for him.

The report also presents reactions to the visit and recalls Sowore’s description of an earlier meeting. Statements about the private conversation are attributed to Sowore’s account, rather than independently established by this briefing.

stories.title: Who paid for the growing Church ? (4)
stories.author: Lanre Ogundipe
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Who paid for the growing Church ? (4)
stories.summary: Lanre Ogundipe continues his examination of the financial foundations of a growing church.
briefing: In the fourth instalment of this series, Lanre Ogundipe considers the resources needed as a religious institution expands. Property, schools, medical work and the support of ministers all bring financial responsibilities.
The column looks beyond contemporary debates about giving to the historical records of institutional funding. Read the full argument and its supporting material in the original column.

stories.title: The tongue, the mind and the throne: Recovering Biblical faith in an age of positive confession
stories.author: Oyewole O. Sarumi
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: The tongue, the mind and the throne: Recovering Biblical faith in an age of positive confession
stories.summary: Oyewole O. Sarumi considers the relationship between biblical faith and positive-confession teaching.
briefing: Oyewole O. Sarumi examines ideas about the power of speech and thought within contemporary Pentecostal and charismatic teaching. The column argues for a distinction between biblical faith and approaches centred on personal fulfilment.
This is the author’s theological commentary. The full essay develops the argument in detail and should be read as an attributed opinion, rather than a newsroom finding about every church or believer.

stories.title: Berean Bible confab advocates need to put faith to work
stories.author: Toyin Adeniyi
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Berean Bible confab advocates need to put faith to work
stories.summary: Speakers at the Berean Bible Conference call for scriptural understanding to become practical action.
briefing: Toyin Adeniyi reports on discussions at the Berean Bible Conference, which brought participants together in person and online. Speakers connected engagement with Scripture to the way Christians respond to contemporary challenges.
The report considers the relationship between learning, spiritual development and purposeful action. The original article includes the speakers’ contributions and further context from the event.

stories.title: Prosperity must reach every Nigerian-CAN
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Prosperity must reach every Nigerian-CAN
stories.summary: CAN’s Independence Day message asks for economic progress to be felt in everyday life.
briefing: The Christian Association of Nigeria’s message to President Bola Tinubu calls for the benefits of economic policy to reach ordinary families. The statement, attributed to CAN president Archbishop Daniel Okoh, discusses the shift from reforms towards prosperity.
Church Times reports on the association’s concerns about living costs, employment, safety and opportunity. The full article presents CAN’s position in the context of its Independence Day message.

stories.title: Deliverance From the Power of Fear
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Deliverance From the Power of Fear
stories.summary: A faith reflection on fear, courage and the language of Scripture.
briefing: This devotional piece explores fear through a Christian reading of Scripture. It distinguishes reverence for God from forms of fear that the writer considers harmful to spiritual life.

The original article develops its teaching through biblical references and categories of fear. It is a faith reflection, not a clinical assessment or a substitute for professional mental-health support.

stories.title: WATS hosts three-day Discipleship Conference, to provide free lunch and materials,
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: WATS hosts three-day Discipleship Conference, to provide free lunch and materials,
stories.summary: West Africa Theological Seminary announces a conference focused on sustainable discipleship.
briefing: West Africa Theological Seminary outlines plans for a three-day conference intended to help church leaders develop discipleship within their congregations. The original announcement identifies Dr D. Z. Cofield and his team as facilitators.

The report gives the programme dates as 14–16 October and describes the resources offered to participants. Confirm attendance arrangements with the organisers using the information in the original report.

stories.title: Nigeria @ 66: Primate Ositelu itemises five reasons to praise God over the country
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Nigeria @ 66: Primate Ositelu itemises five reasons to praise God over the country
stories.summary: Primate Rufus Ositelu offers a thanksgiving perspective on Nigeria’s sixty-sixth anniversary.
briefing: Church Times reports on an anniversary message from Rufus Ositelu, Primate of the Church of the Lord Aladura. Despite Nigeria’s economic difficulties, he proposes reasons for thanksgiving.

The article presents the religious leader’s assessment of the country and his reasons for gratitude. These are attributed reflections, not an independent measure of national security or economic progress.

stories.title: Sola Osunmakinde: When the applause came he gave it away
stories.author: Tosin Olugbenga
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Sola Osunmakinde: When the applause came he gave it away
stories.summary: Tosin Olugbenga reflects on leadership lessons from Pastor Sola Osunmakinde.
briefing: Tosin Olugbenga looks back on experiences at Household of David in Lagos and a moment that shaped his understanding of leadership. The personal reflection recalls the fire that preceded the church’s 2024 Mercy Conference.
The original piece draws lessons from the author’s recollections of Pastor Sola Osunmakinde. Read the full account for its context and the incident behind the headline.

stories.title: I Shall Not Want: Lessons from Psalm 23
stories.author: Gbenga Osinaike
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: I Shall Not Want: Lessons from Psalm 23
stories.summary: Gbenga Osinaike returns to Psalm 23 and the distinction between need and desire.
briefing: In this publisher’s note, Gbenga Osinaike considers how the familiar language of Psalm 23 is interpreted. He questions readings that turn the promise of care into an expectation that every desire will be satisfied.
The piece develops a reflection on provision, contentment and greed. It is the publisher’s theological commentary, with the full argument available in the original note.

stories.title: From Economic Invisibility to Economic Agency: Building the Infrastructure for Africa’s Informal Economy
stories.author: Oyewole Sarumi
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: From Economic Invisibility to Economic Agency: Building the Infrastructure for Africa’s Informal Economy
stories.summary: Oyewole Sarumi looks at financial access and the structures supporting Africa’s informal businesses.
briefing: Oyewole Sarumi uses discussion of a Moniepoint impact report to explore what formal finance can mean for businesses operating in the informal economy. The commentary argues that headline lending figures tell only part of the story.

The essay examines the relationship between financial services and economic participation. Numerical claims remain those presented in the source article and report; this briefing does not independently audit them.

stories.title: The Great OOSC Number Reset? – Examining the Kaduna Household Mapping Model for Counting Out-of-School Children
stories.author: Oyewole Sarumi
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: The Great OOSC Number Reset? – Examining the Kaduna Household Mapping Model for Counting Out-of-School Children
stories.summary: Oyewole Sarumi questions the methods behind counting Nigeria’s out-of-school children.
briefing: Oyewole Sarumi examines the proposed use of Kaduna’s household-mapping approach to identify children outside education. The commentary distinguishes an appealing policy headline from the details of a counting method.

The essay asks who is included, how a child’s status is defined, and whether vulnerable children outside conventional households are captured. Its focus is the quality and implications of education data.

stories.title: Tackling corruption in Nigeria’s Healthcare System
stories.author: Aderinola Adeogun
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Tackling corruption in Nigeria’s Healthcare System
stories.summary: Aderinola Adeogun examines accountability, public trust and the human cost of healthcare failures.
briefing: Aderinola Adeogun discusses the pressures on Nigeria’s healthcare system, including funding, staffing, infrastructure and accountability. The article frames these issues through the experiences of people seeking treatment.
The original report considers corruption and systemic failures as obstacles to access. Its specific accounts and allegations should be read with their original attribution and context.

stories.title: Corruption in the Education System: Need for transparency in disbursement of NELFUND
stories.author: Aderinola Adeogun
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Corruption in the Education System: Need for transparency in disbursement of NELFUND
stories.summary: A report on student concerns and calls for greater accountability in education-loan disbursement.
briefing: Aderinola Adeogun examines concerns raised by students about tuition payments through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund. The report describes allegations of differences between approved amounts and institutional records.
The article calls for transparency and an examination of the disbursement process. Allegations remain attributed to the accounts in the original report; this briefing does not determine wrongdoing.

stories.title: Eternal salvation and the online debate
stories.author: Gbenga Osinaike
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Eternal salvation and the online debate
stories.summary: The publisher considers the tone and substance of an online argument about eternal salvation.
briefing: Gbenga Osinaike responds to a social-media debate about whether salvation can be lost. He describes how a pastor’s remarks prompted increasingly heated exchanges online.
The note considers the language of the argument alongside its theological question. Read the full piece for the publisher’s analysis and conclusion.

stories.title: Man can only provide security; only God guarantees safety, says Ven. Lt Col. Olusada @ 50
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Man can only provide security; only God guarantees safety, says Ven. Lt Col. Olusada @ 50
stories.summary: An Anglican priest and army officer reflects on service, gratitude and turning fifty.
briefing: Church Times speaks with Olufemi Olusada following his fiftieth-birthday celebration in Ogun State. The introduction describes a gathering of family, friends and members of the church community.
The interview brings together his experiences as a military officer and an Anglican priest. Read the original questions and answers for his views on security, safety and faith.

stories.title: Antimalarial drugs and Vitamin c combination
stories.author: Oluwatise Osinaike
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Antimalarial drugs and Vitamin c combination
stories.summary: A pharmacy-focused discussion of questions surrounding antimalarial treatment and vitamin C.
briefing: Oluwatise Osinaike draws on community-pharmacy experience to discuss questions about taking vitamin C during antimalarial treatment. The article describes an individual encounter and considers factors that may affect a patient’s response to medication.

For treatment decisions, consult a qualified clinician or pharmacist. This briefing identifies the subject of the published article; it does not establish a universal interaction or recommend changing prescribed medication.

stories.title: Why Church of the Lord Aladura is Scandal-Free – Primate Ositelu
stories.author: Church Times
stories.imageAlt: Featured image from the original Church Times Nigeria article: Why Church of the Lord Aladura is Scandal-Free – Primate Ositelu
stories.summary: Rufus Ositelu discusses the history, leadership and character of the Church of the Lord Aladura.
briefing: The interview explores the Church of the Lord Aladura’s history and the account of its founder offered by current Primate Rufus Ositelu. It places the conversation in the context of the church’s centenary.
The headline’s description is an attributed claim from the interviewee. The original conversation provides his perspective on leadership, governance and the denomination’s development.
